source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental course, principle, or order of reality; the central Daoist notion of the ultimate way things are and should proceed.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often refers to an ineffable, governing principle rather than a specific road or method.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text and broader pre-Qin usage
Sentence Translations (English): The great Way can be followed; it is not made by human effort.
The sage keeps to the Way and does not dare to go before the world.
Few know the Way, but many trust it.
The Way lies within heaven and earth, pervading everywhere.
Sentences: 聖人守道，不敢為天下先。
道在天地之中，無所不貫。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical road, path, or route of travel.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Refers to an actual route rather than an abstract principle.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; common in received pre-Qin and Han usage
Sentence Translations (English): There was a road ahead, and travelers had to go by it.
The road was blocked, so carriages and horses all stopped.
The guest asked the official about the road.
At dusk he crossed a mountain path, where wind and snow were severe.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A method, procedure, or means by which something is done or achieved.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focuses on an effective course of action rather than moral principle or literal road.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; broader pre-Qin and Han usage
Sentence Translations (English): A well-governed state has a method; a chaotic state has none.
By learning the ancients' method, one can accomplish things.
Its method is easy to understand, so the crowd follows it.
In military affairs, the key method lies in judging the right moment.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To express something in words or discourse, or to treat it as an object of verbal explanation. In this line it is the first 道, used verbally before 道 as a noun.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Takes an object and refers to verbal articulation rather than the Dao as a substantive principle.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text as transmitted with Wang Bi commentary
